subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on operating systems and translators, then mark my answer against the CCEA spec.
promptWeak: Explain system software, operating systems and translators for GCSE CCEA Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of application software?
questions.explain: Application software lets the user carry out specific tasks; a word processor is a classic example. The others are system software.

questions.q: What is the main role of system software?
options: To run and manage the computer and its hardware
To let the user write essays
questions.explain: System software (such as the operating system and utilities) runs and controls the computer itself, providing a platform for applications to run on.

questions.q: A student lists: operating system, spreadsheet, web browser, photo editor. How many are application software?
questions.explain: The spreadsheet, web browser and photo editor are applications (3). The operating system is system software.

questions.q: Which task is application software designed for?
options: Managing the CPU and memory directly
Helping the user complete a specific job such as editing a document
questions.explain: Application software is written to help the user complete particular tasks, like editing documents, browsing the web or editing images.

questions.q: Which of these is a function of an operating system?
options: Managing hardware, memory, files and user interface
questions.explain: The operating system manages the computer's resources, including hardware, memory, files, processes and the user interface.

questions.q: When you run several programs at once, which OS function decides how CPU time is shared between them?
questions.explain: The operating system's process management schedules CPU time so multiple programs can appear to run at the same time.

questions.q: What does the operating system's memory management do?
options: Allocates areas of memory (RAM) to programs and reclaims it when finished
questions.explain: Memory management allocates RAM to running programs, keeps them from interfering with each other, and frees memory when a program closes.

questions.q: What does GUI stand for?
questions.explain: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface: an interface using windows, icons, menus and pointers so users interact visually rather than typing commands.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of a graphical user interface (GUI) over a command line interface?
options: It is easier for beginners because it is visual and intuitive
questions.explain: A GUI is usually easier for non-experts because it is visual and intuitive, though it typically uses more memory and processing power than a command line.

questions.q: Which task is part of the operating system's file management?
options: Creating, saving, renaming and organising files in folders
questions.explain: File management lets users and programs create, name, save, move, copy, delete and organise files and folders on storage.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of utility software?
questions.explain: Utility software performs maintenance and housekeeping tasks; antivirus and disk clean-up tools are typical examples.

questions.q: What does disk defragmentation utility software do?
options: Reorganises fragmented files so they are stored contiguously, improving access speed
questions.explain: Defragmentation rearranges scattered (fragmented) parts of files so they are stored together, letting the drive read them more quickly.

questions.q: Which utility would you use to reduce the file size of a large folder before emailing it?
questions.explain: A file compression utility (e.g. a zip tool) reduces the total size of files so they are quicker to send or take up less storage.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a translator?
options: To convert program source code into machine code the CPU can run
questions.explain: A translator converts program code written by a programmer into machine code (binary) that the processor can execute.

questions.q: Which three types of translator are covered by the specification?
questions.explain: The three translators are the compiler and interpreter (for high-level languages) and the assembler (for assembly language).

questions.q: How does a compiler work?
options: It converts machine code back to English
It translates one line at a time as the program runs
It translates the whole program into machine code in one go before it runs
questions.explain: A compiler translates the entire source program into machine code in one step, producing an executable file that can then be run on its own.

questions.q: How does an interpreter differ from a compiler?
options: It works only with assembly language
It translates and runs the code one instruction at a time
It produces a permanent executable file
questions.explain: An interpreter translates and executes the source code line by line each time it runs, without producing a separate executable file.

questions.q: Why can an interpreter be useful when developing and testing a program?
options: It runs faster than compiled code
It stops at the first error and reports it, making debugging easier
questions.explain: Because an interpreter runs code line by line, it halts and reports the first error it meets, which helps a programmer locate and fix bugs quickly.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of compiled code once it has been produced?
options: It runs quickly and can be distributed without the source code
It must be translated again every time it runs
It needs the compiler present to run
questions.explain: Compiled code runs quickly because it is already in machine code, and the executable can be shared without giving away the source code.

questions.q: What does an assembler translate?
options: High-level language such as Python into machine code
questions.explain: An assembler translates low-level assembly language (which uses mnemonics) into the machine code the CPU can execute.
